title: Hang a planter by its ring on a wall bracket's hook, clear of the table, and let go
instruction: Hang the planter on the wall hook by its ring so it hangs clear of the table, and let go of it.
context: Hanging a planter, bird feeder or lantern on a bracket hook is something most gardeners and renters do. The load hangs from a ring that must be lifted over the hook's upturned tip, moved in along the bar and let down so the bar takes the weight; carried by its ring the pot swings, so the hand has to wait before moving in. Let go short of the tip and the planter drops; hang it so the pot touches the wall or the ground and it chafes and gets knocked. The job is done when it hangs from the bar, clear, and is still with nobody holding it.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top (z 0); arm bases at y +305 mm and -305 mm. (1) A wall panel: 20 mm plywood, 500 mm wide (y -50 to +450 mm), 320 mm tall, standing fixed on the table, its face toward the robot at x 430 mm. (2) A plant bracket screwed to the panel's face at y 200 mm: a steel plate 50 mm wide, 80 mm tall, 6 mm thick, centred z 190 mm, and a round steel bar 8 mm thick, axis z 190 mm, projecting 150 mm from the plate toward the robot (x 424 down to 274 mm). At the bar's free end an upturned lip: an 8 mm round post centred x 278 mm, its top 10 mm above the bar's top (z 204 mm). The bracket is fixed. (3) A planter: a 4 in galvanized steel pail, 100 mm across its rim, 80 mm tall, holding 170 g of dry sand in a zip bag, 0.25 kg in all, with a 4 mm steel wire bail: a U 106 mm wide (centre lines) hinged on two ears on the rim (axis along y, 76 mm above the pot's base), rising 48 mm to a top bar. A 2 in zinc-plated welded steel ring (5 mm wire, 40 mm hole, 50 mm outside, 22 g) is linked through the bail's top bar, plane along y, hole facing x, standing upright over the bail. The pot stands on the table at x 250 mm, y 100 mm; the ring's centre is 146.5 mm above the table. Hung, the ring's upper wire rests on the bar's top behind the lip, its centre 16 mm below the bar's axis (z 174 mm), the bail and ring plumb above the pot, and the pot's base is 27.5 mm above the table. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read on the last control step from the planter's pose and both grippers. Ring on the bar: the bar passes through the ring's hole behind the lip: the hole's axis within 60 degrees of the bar's (x), the bar's axis crossing the ring's plane within 20 mm of the ring's centre, that crossing between x 287 and 419 mm, and the ring's centre at least 8 mm below the bar's axis (hung it is 16 mm below). Clear: the pot's lowest point 20 mm or more above the table top and its rim 3 mm or more short of the wall panel (x 427 mm): nothing but the ring touches it. Plumb: the pot's axis within 10 degrees of vertical. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones (the pads and 38 mm of finger) are 30 mm or more from every part of the planter. Still: over the last 1 s the pot's base centre and the ring's centre each move under 5 mm from where they were at its start, and the pot and the ring each turn under 5 degrees. Score 0 if the pot ever falls off the table (its lowest point more than 20 mm below the table top), and 0 unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 ring on the bar, clear, plumb, still; 0.5 ring on the bar and clear but leaning or still swinging; 0.25 ring on the bar but the pot touching or within 20 mm of the table, or within 3 mm of the wall; 0 otherwise (ring not on the bar: dropped, short of the lip, held up beside the bar, pot back on the table). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial: side view with a rule for the bar through the hole, the ring behind the lip and the ring 8 mm below the bar; a rule from the table to the pot's lowest edge (20 mm) and a 3 mm spacer to the wall; front and side photos against a card ruled with a 10 mm grid and level lines, the rim's line measured with a protractor on the photo (10 degrees; nothing is added to the planter); the video of the last second against the same card (5 mm, and the rim's line turning under 5 degrees between its first and last frames); a 30 mm spacer block against each hand.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, the simulator's default friction. The pot is a solid cylinder (a real pail is hollow with 170 g of sand). The bail is a rigid U on ear hinges and the ring a rigid octagon on a hinge at its apex, each with a light spring toward upright, standing in for pinched ears and a soft-wire binding; no chain (a ring and three chains cannot be one articulation). The lip is a straight post, the ring an octagon.
reset_notes: Stand the pot on its taped mark (x 250 mm, y 100 mm), the bail upright (its ears pinched so it stands by friction), the ring upright on the apex (bound with two turns of 1 mm soft iron wire), hole facing the wall. Weigh the planter: 0.25 kg plus or minus 10 g; top up the sand if any spilled. Check the bracket is tight and its bar level. Nothing is consumed; about 1 minute.
